hook: Last video's quiz answer: two lakh eighty-seven thousand five hundred rupees. Well done if you got it!
Now, C B S E Class Eleven. T. S. Graywaal, Question thirty-six.
This trial balance hides two adjustments that are not in the list.
Can you spot them? Let's solve it together.
question: Here is the question. The trial balance of Karman, on thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
Debit side: opening stock, purchases, freight, wages, salaries and other expenses, investments, debtors, bad debts, building, machinery, furniture, commission, insurance, and bank.
Credit side: capital, sales, creditors, discount received, provision for doubtful debts, and interest on investments.
Both sides total thirty-four lakh forty-five thousand rupees.
Now read two items carefully. Wages, for eleven months up to February. And insurance, up to thirty-first July, twenty twenty-six.
adjust: One. Closing stock, two lakh twenty-five thousand rupees.
Two. Machinery of forty-five thousand, purchased on first October, twenty twenty-five, was shown as purchases. Freight on it, five thousand, is included in freight on purchases.
Three. Commission is payable at two and a half percent on sales.
Four. Investments were sold at ten percent profit, but the proceeds were credited to sales account.
Five. Write off further bad debts of ten thousand, and maintain provision for doubtful debts at five percent of debtors.
Six. Depreciate building by two and a half percent, and machinery and furniture at ten percent per annum.
Pause the video, and try it yourself. Then check with me.
hidden: Wages, sixty-six thousand, are for eleven months only, up to February. So March wages are still outstanding.
Sixty-six thousand into one, over eleven. Six thousand rupees outstanding. Total wages, seventy-two thousand.
Insurance, twenty-four thousand, is paid up to thirty-first July, twenty twenty-six. That is four months into next year.
Twenty-four thousand into four, over twelve. Eight thousand rupees prepaid. Insurance expense, sixteen thousand.
Outstanding wages is a liability, and prepaid insurance is an asset in the balance sheet.
a1: Adjustment two. Machinery shown as purchases.
Buying machinery is capital expenditure, not a purchase of goods.
So deduct forty-five thousand from purchases. Fifteen lakh ninety-five thousand becomes fifteen lakh fifty thousand.
And deduct the freight of five thousand from freight on purchases. Twenty-five thousand becomes twenty thousand.
Add both to machinery. Five lakh, plus forty-five thousand, plus five thousand. Five lakh fifty thousand.
a2: Investments cost one lakh. Sold at ten percent profit, so the proceeds are one lakh ten thousand.
These proceeds were wrongly credited to sales. Deduct them. Twenty-three lakh ten thousand becomes twenty-two lakh.
Profit on sale of investments, ten thousand, is credited to profit and loss.
All investments are sold, so investments are nil in the balance sheet.
a3: Two and a half percent on the corrected sales of twenty-two lakh. Fifty-five thousand rupees.
Already paid, forty-five thousand. So ten thousand is outstanding.
Debit profit and loss with fifty-five thousand, and show outstanding commission of ten thousand as a liability.
a4: Adjustment five. Bad debts and provision.
Debtors, two lakh fifty thousand, less further bad debts of ten thousand. Two lakh forty thousand.
New provision at five percent. Two lakh forty thousand into five, over hundred. Twelve thousand.
Charge to profit and loss: fifteen thousand, plus ten thousand, plus twelve thousand. Thirty-seven thousand.
Less the old provision of eight thousand. Twenty-nine thousand rupees.
In the balance sheet, debtors two lakh forty thousand, less provision twelve thousand. Two lakh twenty-eight thousand.
a5: Building at two and a half percent. Three lakh into two point five, over hundred. Seven thousand five hundred.
Old machinery at ten percent. Five lakh into ten, over hundred. Fifty thousand.
The new machine of fifty thousand was bought on first October, so only six months. Fifty thousand into ten over hundred, into six over twelve. Two thousand five hundred.
Furniture at ten percent. Four thousand.
Total depreciation, sixty-four thousand rupees, goes to profit and loss.
trading: Now the trading account of Karman, for the year ended thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
To purchases, fifteen lakh ninety-five thousand, less machinery forty-five thousand. Fifteen lakh fifty thousand.
To freight on purchases, twenty-five thousand, less five thousand. Twenty thousand.
To wages, sixty-six thousand, plus outstanding six thousand. Seventy-two thousand.
Credit side. By sales, twenty-three lakh ten thousand, less sale of investments one lakh ten thousand. Twenty-two lakh.
By closing stock, two lakh twenty-five thousand. Total, twenty-four lakh twenty-five thousand.
Gross profit, seven lakh eight thousand rupees.
pl: Next, the profit and loss account.
Credit side. Gross profit, seven lakh eight thousand. Discount received, fifteen thousand.
Interest on investments, twelve thousand. Profit on sale of investments, ten thousand. Total, seven lakh forty-five thousand.
Debit side. Salaries, one lakh forty thousand. Postages and courier, twelve thousand.
Printing and stationery, eighteen thousand. Miscellaneous expenses, thirty thousand.
Bad debts and provision, twenty-nine thousand.
Commission, forty-five thousand plus ten thousand. Fifty-five thousand.
Insurance, twenty-four thousand less eight thousand. Sixteen thousand.
Depreciation. Building seven thousand five hundred, machinery fifty-two thousand five hundred, furniture four thousand. Sixty-four thousand.
Net profit, three lakh eighty-one thousand rupees.
bs: Finally, the balance sheet of Karman, as at thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
Capital, eight lakh. Add net profit, three lakh eighty-one thousand. Less drawings, sixty thousand. Eleven lakh twenty-one thousand.
Sundry creditors, three lakh. Outstanding wages, six thousand. Outstanding commission, ten thousand.
Liabilities total, fourteen lakh thirty-seven thousand.
Assets. Building, two lakh ninety-two thousand five hundred. Machinery, five lakh fifty thousand, less fifty-two thousand five hundred. Four lakh ninety-seven thousand five hundred.
Furniture, thirty-six thousand. Closing stock, two lakh twenty-five thousand.
Sundry debtors, two lakh twenty-eight thousand. Prepaid insurance, eight thousand. Bank balance, one lakh fifty thousand.
Assets total, fourteen lakh thirty-seven thousand. The balance sheet tallies!
traps: Four exam traps from this question.
Trap one. Read the trial balance headings. Wages for eleven months, and insurance up to July, are hidden adjustments.
Trap two. Machinery and its freight were wrongly in purchases. Remove both from the trading account, and add them to machinery.
Trap three. Calculate commission on the corrected sales of twenty-two lakh, not twenty-three lakh ten thousand.
Trap four. The new machine was bought on first October. Charge depreciation for six months only.
recap: Gross profit, seven lakh eight thousand.
Net profit, three lakh eighty-one thousand.
Balance sheet total, fourteen lakh thirty-seven thousand, on both sides.
Remember: always read the trial balance headings for hidden adjustments.
